name: Caius Marcius Coriolanus
description: Rome's greatest soldier, surnamed Coriolanus for single-handedly storming the Volscian city of Corioli. Magnificent in battle but contemptuous of the common people, he cannot bend his pride to beg the citizens for the consulship; banished from Rome, he turns traitor and leads his old enemy's army against his own city, until his mother's pleading stops him and costs him his life. (Labelled MARCIUS until Act 1 ends and he is given the name Coriolanus.)

relationships.relation: rival of, later ally and victim of

name: Menenius Agrippa
description: An old patrician, witty and genial, a fatherly friend and champion of Coriolanus. He pacifies the mutinous citizens with his fable of the belly and the members, mediates between the patricians and the tribunes, and is heartbroken when the banished Coriolanus turns him away from the Volscian camp.

name: Volumnia
description: Coriolanus's formidable mother, who raised him to prize honour and wounds above life itself. Fiercely ambitious for him, she at last kneels before him in the Volscian camp and, in the play's turning point, persuades him to spare Rome, knowing the mercy may doom him.

name: Tullus Aufidius
description: General of the Volscians and Coriolanus's great rival, who has fought and lost to him many times. When the banished Coriolanus comes to him in disguise, Aufidius embraces him as a brother-in-arms; then, eclipsed and resentful in his own city, he brands him a traitor and engineers his murder.

relationships.relation: rival of, then host and killer of

name: Sicinius Velutus
description: One of the two newly created tribunes of the people. Shrewd and demagogic, he and Brutus turn the citizens against Coriolanus and engineer his banishment, then quail when news comes that his vengeance is marching on Rome.

name: Junius Brutus
description: One of the two tribunes of the people (a namesake, not the Brutus of Julius Caesar). With Sicinius he speaks for the plebeians, goading Coriolanus into the contemptuous outburst that gets him banished.

name: Cominius
description: The Roman general and consul under whom Coriolanus serves at Corioli. A steady, admiring patron, he reports Coriolanus's valour to the Senate and later pleads with him, in vain, to spare Rome.

name: Virgilia
description: Coriolanus's quiet, loving wife, his 'gracious silence,' who dreads the wars that her husband and mother-in-law glory in. Her tears in the Volscian camp help move him to mercy.

name: Titus Lartius
description: A Roman general who fights beside Coriolanus at Corioli and is left to govern the captured city.

name: Valeria
description: A noble Roman lady, friend to Virgilia and Volumnia, who joins them in the embassy that begs Coriolanus to spare Rome. Coriolanus calls her 'the moon of Rome.'

name: Young Marcius
description: Coriolanus and Virgilia's young son, who already shares his father's fierce temper. He comes with the women to the Volscian camp.

name: Gentlewoman
description: A waiting-woman who attends Virgilia.

name: First Citizen
description: A leader of the mutinous Roman commoners in the opening scene, and one of the plebeians whose 'voices' Coriolanus must beg for the consulship.

name: Second Citizen
description: One of the Roman commoners; in the opening riot more mindful of Coriolanus's past services than the First Citizen.

name: Third Citizen
description: One of the Roman citizens in the marketplace who grant, then withdraw, their voices for Coriolanus's consulship.

name: Fourth Citizen
description: One of the Roman citizens debating Coriolanus's bid for the consulship in the marketplace.

name: Fifth Citizen
description: One of the Roman citizens debating Coriolanus's bid for the consulship in the marketplace.

name: Sixth Citizen
description: One of the Roman citizens debating Coriolanus's bid for the consulship in the marketplace.

name: Citizens
description: The Roman plebeians speaking as one, the 'many-headed multitude' whose votes and anger Coriolanus despises.

name: All
description: The full company on stage answering in unison, by turns the mutinous citizens, the acclaiming soldiers, or the assembled people.

name: First Senator
description: A presiding senator (Roman, and at Corioli and Antium a senator of the Volscians) who speaks for the council and welcomes the victorious army.

name: Second Senator
description: A senator who speaks in the Roman or Volscian council.

name: Senators
description: The assembled senators speaking together.

name: First Patrician
description: A Roman patrician supporting Coriolanus against the tribunes and the crowd.

name: Second Patrician
description: A Roman patrician supporting Coriolanus against the tribunes and the crowd.

name: Herald
description: The Roman herald who proclaims Coriolanus's triumphant return and his new name before the people.

name: Aedile
description: An officer attending the tribunes, sent to summon the people and, at their command, to arrest Coriolanus.

name: First Officer
description: One of two officers laying cushions in the Capitol, who discuss Coriolanus's worth and his open contempt for the people.

name: Second Officer
description: The second of the two officers in the Capitol who weigh Coriolanus's merits against his pride.

name: First Soldier
description: A soldier in the Roman army before Corioli.

name: Second Soldier
description: A soldier in the Roman army before Corioli.

name: Lieutenant
description: Aufidius's lieutenant, who warns him that Coriolanus is eclipsing him in the soldiers' and the people's affection.

name: Messenger
description: A messenger bearing news between Rome, the camp, and the cities of the war.

name: Second Messenger
description: A second messenger bringing battlefield or city news.

name: Roman (Nicanor)
description: Nicanor, a Roman in the pay of the Volscians, who meets the Volscian agent on the highway and reports that Rome, having banished Coriolanus, is ripe for attack.

name: Volsce (Adrian)
description: Adrian, a Volscian intelligencer who meets the Roman traitor on the road and brings him to Aufidius.

name: Romans
description: Roman soldiers carrying off plunder from the sack of Corioli while Marcius scorns their greed.

name: First Servingman
description: One of Aufidius's serving-men, who first scorn the ragged stranger Coriolanus, then boast of him once he is honoured.

name: Second Servingman
description: One of Aufidius's serving-men in his house at Antium.

name: Third Servingman
description: One of Aufidius's serving-men, who delivers the comic praise of war over peace once Coriolanus is welcomed.

name: First Guard
description: One of the Volscian watchmen at the camp before Rome who refuse the disgraced Menenius entry to Coriolanus.

name: Second Guard
description: One of the Volscian watchmen who turn Menenius away from Coriolanus's tent.

name: First Conspirator
description: One of Aufidius's fellow conspirators who help him cut down Coriolanus at Corioli.

name: Second Conspirator
description: One of Aufidius's fellow conspirators against Coriolanus.

name: Third Conspirator
description: One of Aufidius's fellow conspirators against Coriolanus.

name: Conspirators
description: Aufidius's conspirators speaking together.

name: First Lord
description: One of the lords of the Volscian city who try to protect Coriolanus and mourn his murder.

name: Second Lord
description: One of the Volscian lords who decry Aufidius's murder of Coriolanus.

name: Third Lord
description: One of the Volscian lords who call for Aufidius to answer for the killing.

name: Lords
description: The Volscian lords speaking together.

name: Both Tribunes
description: Sicinius and Brutus speaking together.
